prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After OAuthClientProvider reloads tokens from TokenStorage (e.g. on process restart), token_expiry_time is never restored on the in-memory OAuthToken, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired token as still valid. This skips the existing proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow and forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh on the next request. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After OAuthClientProvider reloads tokens from TokenStorage (e.g. on process restart), token_expiry_time is never restored on the in-memory OAuthToken, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired token as still valid. This skips the existing proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow and forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh on the next request. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's helpers split the entire header into segments and then explicitly match the auth-scheme token (partition on first space, compare 'bearer' case-insensitively) before collecting that challenge's params, directly targeting the substring-match failure mode named in its title (e.g. a scheme or value elsewhere in the header being mistaken for a Bearer parameter). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only splits the substring after the header's first space, which assumes a single-scheme header and does not re-verify the scheme token, so it does not cover the same scheme-disambiguation case that #3041 handles.

members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same root cause in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser split on every comma without regard to quoted auth-param values, so a comma inside a quoted value (e.g. inside error_description) truncated/mis-split parameters, and scheme/field matching was done via naive substring checks instead of proper tokenization.
